findings: The former 150 ms deadline began before sink setup, PTY setup, start-event fsync and Popen. Requiring one marker before that real scheduling deadline was not a deterministic test of marker durability.

The revised fixture retains the actual PTY, original default MarkerObserver and original sink append implementation. It observes successful fsync of stdout and marker-event descriptors and reads the actual expected raw bytes and exactly one marker before selecting the durable-marker trigger.

The test patches only capture.time with a monotonic proxy, not the shared time module. Before a trigger the clock is zero; expired_at is assigned once; after the trigger the clock is PROCESS_SECONDS plus nonnegative real elapsed time. No backward clock jump or frozen cleanup clock was identified.

A missing marker causes the existing finite one-second fixture readiness boundary to trigger timeout and the durable-marker assertion to fail. The fixture does not manufacture an event or classify readiness timeout as a successful marker case.

The original 0.15 configured test process timeout remains asserted. The test additionally checks leader reaping, group kill, no exceeded cleanup deadline and absence of raw stdout/stderr in the terminal process record.
The production collector process/cleanup limits and evidence-admission boundaries are unchanged by the reviewed test repair.
scope: Static causal review of the one fixture repair and its unchanged collector context; not an independent execution receipt or a general scheduler/capture proof.
